Okay, here's how I approached this. The task is to identify five representative, peer-reviewed journal articles on Uses and Gratifications Theory (U&G). My immediate focus is on the *quality* and *relevance* of the articles, given that it's for an expert audience, so I am going for "classic" and foundational, as well as those that represent important evolution and applications. Textbooks and review papers are out; we want the original research or influential empirical application.

First, I had to ensure I understood the explicit requirements: title, authors, year, journal, DOI or URL, and the specified JSON output format. I knew I needed to meticulously populate those fields. I was quite careful to extract exact DOIs, which is critical.

I started by listing potential candidates. Katz, Blumler, and Gurevitch (1973) is the obvious starting point – the seminal piece that really codified the theory. Then Rubin (1984) and (1983) were essential additions, for their work in defining "ritualized" versus "instrumental" viewing, which has been foundational in the field. Palmgreen and Rayburn (1979/1980/1984) were next on my list, given their work on the expectancy-value model within U&G. Ruggiero (2000) was an immediate thought for application of U&G in the Internet age, but I then reconsidered that this might be a review article, rather than "pure" research. Sundar & Limperos (2013) were an obvious next-gen candidate for their work on new media.

I debated whether Ruggiero was too review-y or not, and while it's an important article, I ultimately felt it wasn't the *most* appropriate choice, given the explicit instruction to avoid "review textbooks." I then did a secondary search and vetting of alternative candidates such as Papacharissi & Rubin (2000) and Whiting & Williams (2013) to ensure these are key empirical research papers; I settled on Papacharissi & Rubin as they're a bit more well-known.

Finally, I carefully compiled the references, double-checked each data point, and ensured it matched the required JSON structure precisely, verifying the JSON syntax to ensure valid output.
